Withdrawal event coverage and historical supply reconciliation
Research date: 29 September 2026. This read-only study checks two parts of the existing copied-
Arbitrum withdrawal audit: partitioned event coverage and before/after token supply. It uses the same
fixed PulseChain endpoint, block 27,659,393, hash 
0xc5e582cd902f4bff3b1aa325b9b564fcd5d6dc0ffa77a03fcd105b65c6390275.
Event coverage
The input is the four retained event batches described in the escrow gateway census (Appendix 11), 
specialized gateway history (Appendix 20), and GRT reconciliation (Appendix 12). These collectively
contain 106 receipt-verified WithdrawalFinalized events in 78 transactions, covering ten identified
historical gateway addresses and 91 token addresses.
For every gateway, this batch independently queried the same withdrawal signature in two adjacent,
nonoverlapping ranges:
Blocks 17,233,000 through 22,446,196.
Blocks 22,446,197 through 27,659,393.
All 20 requests returned valid results. The combined event identities match the prior full-range queries
exactly: no missing or additional events. Identity includes emitter address, transaction hash, log
index and block hash. An empty result for a partition was used only after a valid RPC response. This
checks consistency across query partitioning; it does not independently validate the provider's chain
history or cover different event signatures.
Supply reconciliation
The 106 events produce 106 distinct token-and-block pairs. The batch queried totalSupply() for each
token at its withdrawal block and the preceding block: 212 successful, 32-byte return values, with
no reverts or missing results.
Result Number of token/block pairs
Identical before/after supply 104
Positive supply difference 2
Negative supply difference 0
• 
• 
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 134

Result Number of token/block pairs
Missing, reverted or malformed result 0
The two positive differences are:
Token Block Increase in whole-token units
ARB 21,469,490 972,406,600,390,402,296,078,726,88
3,998.977902572465996426
GRT 27,434,949 62,875,936.675361278837595998
Both use 18 decimal places and match the previously identified transaction's mint event and historical
call trace exactly. No other sampled withdrawal block shows a net supply increase for its withdrawn
token.
A block-level difference alone does not attribute a supply change to one transaction: unrelated
transactions in that block can change the same token. Similarly, zero net change alone cannot exclude
offsetting issuance and burning. The separate full trace audit (Appendix 23) examines all 78 actual
transactions and classifies their observed gateway operations. T ogether, these checks strengthen the
distinction between transfer-only withdrawals and the two observed mint executions. Neither check
proves the unobserved source-chain burn or collateral history.
Reproduction
The maintained manifest is Research/experiments/parb_withdrawal_evidence_checks_20260929.json. Run:
python Research/scripts/check_pulsechain_withdrawal_evidence.py \
  --manifest Research/experiments/parb_withdrawal_evidence_checks_20260929.json \
  --output artifacts/parb-withdrawal-evidence-checks-new-run
The script accepts only eth_chainId, eth_getBlockByNumber, eth_getLogs and eth_call, uses no state
overrides, verifies chain 369 and the endpoint header, and rechecks the endpoint after collection. It
refuses to reuse an existing output directory and retains transport errors separately from RPC results.
Raw requests/responses, decoded comparisons and file hashes are in ignored artifacts/parb-withdrawal-
evidence-checks-20260929/. The successful live read-only run, arithmetic assertions, hash checks and Python
compilation validated this research script. Production application code was not changed.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 135
